requirements.original: Variables can be of simple basic types, basic string types, structured types, special data types (including subtypes derived from these types) as well as address, component or default, port or timer types.
requirements.canonical: A variable MAY be of a simple basic type, a basic string type, a structured type, a special data type (including subtypes derived from these types), an address type, a component type, a default type, a port type or a timer type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- Variables can be of simple basic types, basic string types, structured types, special data types (including subtypes derived from these types) as well as address, component or default, port or timer types.

requirements.original: The type of the variable is either provided explicitly or implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing specified in clause 6.5.
requirements.canonical: The type of a variable IS provided either explicitly in the declaration or implicitly according to the automatic typing rules of clause 6.5.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- The type of the variable is either provided explicitly or implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing specified in clause 6.5.

requirements.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part of the declaration is missing and the type of the variable is equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.canonical: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of a variable declaration IS absent.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence names the syntax element TypeOrNestedParDef, but the variable declaration syntax in clauses 11.1 and 11.2 uses TypeOrNestedTypeDef.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part of the declaration is missing and the type of the variable is equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part of the declaration is missing and the type of the variable is equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.canonical: When automatic typing is used, the type of a variable IS equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment in its declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part of the declaration is missing and the type of the variable is equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.original: Variables can be declared and used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
requirements.canonical: A variable MAY be declared and used in testcases, functions and altsteps.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- Variables can be declared and used in test cases, functions and altsteps.

requirements.original: Additionally, variables can be declared in component type definitions.
requirements.canonical: A variable MAY be declared in a component type definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- Additionally, variables can be declared in component type definitions.

requirements.original: These variables can be used in test cases, altsteps and functions which are running on a given component type.
requirements.canonical: A variable declared in a component type definition MAY be used in testcases, altsteps and functions running on that component type.

readings: A variable declared in a component type definition MAY be used in testcases, altsteps and functions whose runs on clause references that component type.
A variable declared in a component type definition MAY be used in testcases, altsteps and functions whose runs on clause references that component type or a component type compatible with it.
ambiguity.issue: 'running on a given component type' does not state whether compatible component types (clause 6.3.3) are included; the first reading is chosen as the literal one.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- These variables can be used in test cases, altsteps and functions which are running on a given component type.

requirements.original: Variables can be declared lazy using the @lazy modifier.
requirements.canonical: A variable MAY be declared lazy using the `@lazy` modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- Variables can be declared lazy using the @lazy modifier.

requirements.original: Alternatively, variables can be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.
requirements.canonical: A variable MAY be declared fuzzy using the `@fuzzy` modifier as an alternative to the `@lazy` modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- Alternatively, variables can be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.

requirements.original: Alternatively, variables can be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.
requirements.canonical: A variable declaration SHALL NOT contain both the `@lazy` and the `@fuzzy` modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- Alternatively, variables can be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.

requirements.original: If a variable is declared fuzzy or lazy they can additionally declared with the @deterministic modifier to indicate that when used in a deterministic evaluation context, any evaluation of the variable would have no side effect and would yield the same result.
requirements.canonical: A variable declared `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` MAY additionally be declared with the `@deterministic` modifier.
requirements.condition: the variable is declared lazy or fuzzy
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- If a variable is declared fuzzy or lazy they can additionally declared with the @deterministic modifier to indicate that when used in a deterministic evaluation context, any evaluation of the variable would have no side effect and would yield the same result.

requirements.original: Lazy and fuzzy features are valid only in the scope, where the variables' names are visible.
requirements.canonical: The lazy or fuzzy property of a variable IS valid only in the scope where the variable name is visible.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- Lazy and fuzzy features are valid only in the scope, where the variables' names are visible.

requirements.original: For example, if a fuzzy variable is passed to a formal parameter declared without a modifier, it loses its fuzzy feature inside the called function.
requirements.canonical: A fuzzy variable passed to a formal parameter declared without a modifier IS not fuzzy inside the called function.
requirements.condition: the fuzzy variable is passed to a formal parameter declared without `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` modifier
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- For example, if a fuzzy variable is passed to a formal parameter declared without a modifier, it loses its fuzzy feature inside the called function.

requirements.original: Similarly, if it is passed to a lazy formal parameter, it becomes lazy within the called function.
requirements.canonical: A fuzzy variable passed to a lazy formal parameter IS lazy within the called function.
requirements.condition: the fuzzy variable is passed to a formal parameter declared `@lazy`
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- Similarly, if it is passed to a lazy formal parameter, it becomes lazy within the called function.

requirements.original: Whenever a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the TE is required to save the lexical environment (the set of directly or indirectly referenced values and templates) valid at the time of the assignment, so that it is possible to resolve the expression at the time of evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy value or template.
requirements.canonical: Whenever a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the test execution SHALL save the lexical environment (the set of directly or indirectly referenced values and templates) valid at the time of the assignment, so that the expression can be resolved when the lazy or fuzzy value or template is evaluated.
requirements.condition: a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- Whenever a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the TE is required to save the lexical environment (the set of directly or indirectly referenced values and templates) valid at the time of the assignment, so that it is possible to resolve the expression at the time of evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy value or template.

requirements.original: If the assignment was made on a lower scope than the evaluation, saving the lexical environment extends lifetime of the referenced variables defined on that lower scope.
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned in a lower scope than the scope of its evaluation, saving the lexical environment IS extending the lifetime of the referenced variables defined in that lower scope.
requirements.condition: the assignment was made in a lower scope than the evaluation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.0 -- If the assignment was made on a lower scope than the evaluation, saving the lexical environment extends lifetime of the referenced variables defined on that lower scope.

requirements.original: It is declared by the var keyword followed by a type identifier or a nested type definition and a variable identifier.
requirements.canonical: A value variable declaration IS the `var` keyword followed by a type identifier or a nested type definition and a variable identifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- It is declared by the var keyword followed by a type identifier or a nested type definition and a variable identifier.

requirements.original: An initial value can be assigned at variable declaration.
requirements.canonical: A value variable declaration MAY assign an initial value to the value variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- An initial value can be assigned at variable declaration.

requirements.original: It may be used at the right hand side as well as at the left hand side of assignments, in expressions, following the return keyword in bodies of functions with a return clause in their headers and may be passed to both value and template-type formal parameters.
requirements.canonical: A value variable MAY be used on the right hand side and on the left hand side of assignments.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- It may be used at the right hand side as well as at the left hand side of assignments, in expressions, following the return keyword in bodies of functions with a return clause in their headers and may be passed to both value and template-type formal parameters.

requirements.original: It may be used at the right hand side as well as at the left hand side of assignments, in expressions, following the return keyword in bodies of functions with a return clause in their headers and may be passed to both value and template-type formal parameters.
requirements.canonical: A value variable MAY be used in expressions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- It may be used at the right hand side as well as at the left hand side of assignments, in expressions, following the return keyword in bodies of functions with a return clause in their headers and may be passed to both value and template-type formal parameters.

requirements.original: It may be used at the right hand side as well as at the left hand side of assignments, in expressions, following the return keyword in bodies of functions with a return clause in their headers and may be passed to both value and template-type formal parameters.
requirements.canonical: A value variable MAY be used following the `return` keyword in the body of a function with a return clause in its header.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- It may be used at the right hand side as well as at the left hand side of assignments, in expressions, following the return keyword in bodies of functions with a return clause in their headers and may be passed to both value and template-type formal parameters.

requirements.original: It may be used at the right hand side as well as at the left hand side of assignments, in expressions, following the return keyword in bodies of functions with a return clause in their headers and may be passed to both value and template-type formal parameters.
requirements.canonical: A value variable MAY be passed as actual parameter to both value formal parameters and template-type formal parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- It may be used at the right hand side as well as at the left hand side of assignments, in expressions, following the return keyword in bodies of functions with a return clause in their headers and may be passed to both value and template-type formal parameters.

requirements.original: var [ ( @lazy | @fuzzy ) [ @deterministic ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] [ ":=" Expression ] [ "," ] }+ [ ";" ]
requirements.canonical: A value variable declaration has the syntax `var` [ ( `@lazy` | `@fuzzy` ) [ `@deterministic` ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] followed by one or more comma-separated VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] [ ":=" Expression ] and an optional ";".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- var [ ( @lazy | @fuzzy ) [ @deterministic ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] [ ":=" Expression ] [ "," ] }+ [ ";" ]

requirements.original: A value variable may change its value during test execution several times.
requirements.canonical: A value variable MAY change its value several times during test execution.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- A value variable may change its value during test execution several times.

requirements.original: A value can be assigned several times to a value variable.
requirements.canonical: A value MAY be assigned several times to a value variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- A value can be assigned several times to a value variable.

requirements.original: The value variable can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: A value variable MAY be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- The value variable can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: a) _Expression shall evaluate to a value which is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef._
requirements.canonical: The Expression in a value variable declaration SHALL evaluate to a value that is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- a) _Expression shall evaluate to a value which is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef._

requirements.original: b) Value variables shall store values only.
requirements.canonical: A value variable SHALL store values only.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- b) Value variables shall store values only.

requirements.original: c) Value variables shall not be declared or used in a module definitions part (i.e. global variables are not supported in TTCN-3).
requirements.canonical: A value variable SHALL NOT be declared or used in a module definitions part.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- c) Value variables shall not be declared or used in a module definitions part (i.e. global variables are not supported in TTCN-3).

requirements.original: c) Value variables shall not be declared or used in a module definitions part (i.e. global variables are not supported in TTCN-3).
requirements.canonical: A global variable IS NOT supported in TTCN-3.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- c) Value variables shall not be declared or used in a module definitions part (i.e. global variables are not supported in TTCN-3).

requirements.original: d) Use of uninitialized value variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: Use of an uninitialized value variable at any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement, or an actual parameter passed to a formal parameter SHALL cause an error.

readings: Use of an uninitialized value variable in any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement or an actual parameter SHALL cause an error (static or dynamic).
Use of an uninitialized value variable in any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement or an actual parameter SHALL cause a dynamic error at runtime only.
ambiguity.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not stated; the canonical text keeps the generic 'error'. Also unclear whether passing to an in formal parameter is excluded from the error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- d) Use of uninitialized value variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.

requirements.original: e) The initialization or assignment of a fuzzy or lazy variable shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.
requirements.canonical: The initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy value variable SHALL NOT contain a call of a function with `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- e) The initialization or assignment of a fuzzy or lazy variable shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.

requirements.original: The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.
requirements.canonical: A function called in the initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy value variable MAY internally call other functions with `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.

requirements.original: f) If a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the expression assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in a deterministic context (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or the initialization of a global non-fuzzy template), the variable SHALL be declared `@deterministic`.
requirements.condition: a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in a deterministic context
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- f) If a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the expression assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.original: f) If a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the expression assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in a deterministic context, the expression assigned to the variable SHALL fulfil the restrictions on the content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.condition: a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in a deterministic context
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- f) If a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the expression assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.original: Evaluation of such an expression shall cause a dynamic error.
requirements.canonical: Evaluation of an expression assigned to a lazy or fuzzy variable that directly or indirectly references that variable SHALL cause a dynamic error.
requirements.condition: the expression assigned to a lazy or fuzzy variable contains a direct or indirect reference to that variable
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- Evaluation of such an expression shall cause a dynamic error.

requirements.original: h) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clauses 6.2.7 and 6.2.3.0) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: Using the dot notation or the index notation to reference a field, alternative or element of an address value whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.condition: the actual value of the address value is `null`
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- h) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clauses 6.2.7 and 6.2.3.0) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.

requirements.original: i) The expression shall evaluate to a value, which is at least partially initialized.
requirements.canonical: The Expression in a value variable declaration SHALL evaluate to a value that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- i) The expression shall evaluate to a value, which is at least partially initialized.

requirements.original: j) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" Expression) shall be present.
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a value variable declaration, the ArrayDef part SHALL be missing as well.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- j) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" Expression) shall be present.

requirements.original: j) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" Expression) shall be present.
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a value variable declaration, the assignment part (":=" Expression) SHALL be present.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- j) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" Expression) shall be present.

requirements.original: var timer v_timer1; ... timer t_myTimer1; ... v_timer1 := t_myTimer1;
requirements.canonical: A value variable of timer type IS assignable from a timer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.1 -- var timer v_timer1; ... timer t_myTimer1; ... v_timer1 := t_myTimer1;
